title: Virtual Event Planning Platform: Mexico deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Add tax and duty explicitly; never bury them in a price. Check with a local expert.
One measure per week: enquiries, orders or revenue; pick one.
Local caution: A large country: start in one city, test one offer, then grow.
A large market with strong regional differences. Start in one city and one niche.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: A monthly review: what we planned, what happened, what we change.
Cluster G, Money services (regulated): Regulated money services; plan as a partner of a licensed firm only. Check with a local expert.
Partner with a host, a tech support person and a speaker network.
Employers register staff for social security and pay the year-end bonus; budget both.

questions.q: In "Register and license Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write MXN next to every number.
Issue electronic invoices as the tax rules require; learn the tool before the first customer. Check with a local expert.
Contribution per unit = price minus the cost of each unit.
A monthly review: what we planned, what happened, what we change.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Customers may ask to see, correct, remove or object to use of their data; set a reply time.
Some activities need extra licences (food, health, tourism, money); list yours before the first order. Check with a local expert.
Choose one event type, such as training days or product demos, and one buyer group.
Work out cost per event and fees.

questions.q: In "Find and serve customers Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Partner with a technical college or business chamber to find helpers and to practise.
Channels: messaging apps, social media and marketplaces; local fairs and markets for a first test.
Keep a list of every tool that stores customer data, including messaging apps.
Launch with a go or no-go rule: 3 paid events in 6 weeks at 60% attendance. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Price, tax and money Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Hold attendee data lightly: name, email, ticket; delete lists after a set time.
Staff may share in profits; small and new firms can differ, so read the rule before you hire. Check with a local expert.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?
Keep a risk list with a response for each; include a rules change. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "People and partners Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Register with the tax authority (a tax ID) before you invoice; choose sole trader or company. Check with a local expert.
One measure per week: enquiries, orders or revenue; pick one.
A simplified small-taxpayer regime may fit a first year; read the current limits.
Written contracts and signed copies for every helper, even part-time.

questions.q: In "Launch plan and review Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Electronic invoices are part of daily trade: learn them in week one.
A simplified small-taxpayer regime may fit a first year; read the current limits.
Keep a risk list with a response for each; include a rules change. Check with a local expert.
Work out cost per event and fees.
